title: Did An AI Just Solve The Riemann Hypothesis?
sources: Anthropic / Levent Alpöge claim of a machine-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis (reported Nov 20-21, 2026: Phys.org, NYT, TechCrunch, Scientific American)
Riemann hypothesis: unsolved since 1859, one of Clay Mathematics Institute's $1,000,000 Millennium Prize Problems
Tom's Hardware / Google Trends: 'Riemann hypothesis solved' searches up 1000%+ in 24 hours after the claim

lines.text: Did an AI just solve the hardest math problem in the world?
lines.caps: DID AN *AI | JUST *SOLVE | THE HARDEST *MATH | PROBLEM IN THE *WORLD?

lines.text: The Riemann hypothesis, open for 167 years.
It's the secret rule that decides where prime numbers hide.
Solve it, and you win one million dollars.
Now a mathematician at Anthropic claims he proved it with Claude, an AI.
lines.caps: A MATH *GENIUS | AND *CLAUDE, | AN *AI | SAY THEY *PROVED IT

lines.text: A proof that has eluded every genius for over a century.
But here's the twist: a human claimed the exact same thing the same week.
Now there are two dueling proofs, human versus machine.
Mathematicians say it's almost certainly true.
But it's not confirmed yet: one wrong step and it all collapses.
So did an AI just solve the hardest math problem in the world yet?
